output_json.patch_notes: Added a private helper `assertWithinDestination(File destination, File target, String entryName)` to AbstractUnArchiver that canonicalizes both paths and throws ArchiverException unless target.equals(destination) or target is nested under destination (startsWith(destPath + File.separator)). Called it right after `final File f = FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName);` in extractFile(), before the overwrite check, dirF.mkdirs(), symlink creation, directory creation, and FileOutputStream write — i.e. before every sink reachable from that resolved path. No other call sites needed changes since both TarUnArchiver.execute() and AbstractZipUnArchiver's extractFileIfIncluded() already call this shared extractFile() method. Added PathTraversalExtractionTest.java with two tests (tar and zip) building a malicious archive with entry name "../escaped-*-marker.txt" and asserting extraction throws ArchiverException and no file lands outside the destination directory.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk: the added check only rejects entries whose resolved canonical path falls outside the destination directory — a case that was never a legitimate use (valid archives always extract within dest). Confirmed no behavioral regression via the full existing test suite (151/151 pass), including SymlinkTest, which specifically exercises symlink entries whose *link target* points outside the destination — that behavior is preserved because the fix only validates the entry's own resolved file location (f), not the symlink target, since constraining the symlink target broke that pre-existing, intentionally-supported test. A more aggressive fix could also validate symlink targets and directory-entry mkdirs targets identically to file entries, but that would require a product decision about whether cross-directory symlinks are supported functionality (current tests say yes) versus a hardening opportunity — flagging this as a possible follow-up but out of scope for a minimal fix that preserves existing behavior.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal ("tar slip"/"zip slip") in plexus-archiver's shared extraction sink, AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile(). The method resolved archive-controlled entryName via FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) with no containment check before the overwrite check, parent-directory creation (mkdirs), and FileOutputStream write. Added a canonical-path containment check (assertWithinDestination) immediately after the resolve, before any of those three sinks, throwing ArchiverException when the resolved target is not equal to or nested under the destination directory. Both TarUnArchiver and AbstractZipUnArchiver (including its Unicode-extra-field entry name path) funnel through this exact method, so the single fix covers every trace in the alert plus same-class bypass variants (../, nested ../../, absolute paths, backslash traversal) since canonicalization normalizes them all. Verified the provided POV now exits 1 (contained) instead of 0 (escaped). I also tried adding a containment check on symlink link targets (mentioned as a related sink in the finder evidence), but reverted it after confirming it broke the project's own SymlinkTest, which intentionally creates/extracts symlinks pointing outside the destination directory as existing supported behavior — that sink is outside the alert's actual traces, so the fix stays scoped to the entryName resolution sink shared by all reported traces. Added a regression test (PathTraversalExtractionTest) exercising both a malicious tar entry and a malicious zip entry named "../escaped-marker.txt" through the real TarUnArchiver/ZipUnArchiver public APIs, asserting ArchiverException is thrown and no file is written outside the destination directory. Full mvn test suite: 151/151 passing (149 pre-existing + 2 new), BUILD SUCCESS.
